subproblem.title: The chord between two distinct, non-antipodal unit vectors stays in the closed unit ball and meets every line through 0 at most once (parent steps 1–2)
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ and let a, b ∈ ℝ^P (Euclid P) with |a| = |b| = 1, a ≠ b and b ≠ −a. Then there are ℓ ∈ ℝ and u ∈ ℝ^P such that ℓ > 0, |a − b| = ℓ, |u| = 1, b + ℓu = a, |b + su| ≤ 1 for every s ∈ [0, ℓ], and, for every e ∈ ℝ^P and s₁, s₂, t₁, t₂ ∈ ℝ, b + s₁u = t₁e and b + s₂u = t₂e imply s₁ = s₂ (the line s ↦ b + su meets each line ℝe through 0 in at most one parameter).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (a b : Euclid P), ‖a‖ = 1 → ‖b‖ = 1 → a ≠ b → b ≠ -a → ∃ (ℓ : ℝ) (u : Euclid P), 0 < ℓ ∧ ‖a - b‖ = ℓ ∧ ‖u‖ = 1 ∧ b + ℓ • u = a ∧ (∀ s ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) ℓ, ‖b + s • u‖ ≤ 1) ∧ ∀ (e : Euclid P) (s₁ s₂ t₁ t₂ : ℝ), b + s₁ • u = t₁ • e → b + s₂ • u = t₂ • e → s₁ = s₂
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof steps 1–2 (the chord [[b, a]] of the pairing argument), Simon 7.3.3, proof of (2), formula (10) (chapter-07.txt lines 563–566: "it is easy to check that such a 1-dimensional minimizing cone necessarily has the form m[[ℓ]]").
1. (Choice of ℓ and u.) Put ℓ := |a − b| and u := ℓ⁻¹(a − b). Since a ≠ b we have a − b ≠ 0, hence ℓ > 0 (norm_pos_iff), and |a − b| = ℓ holds by definition.
2. (Unit direction, endpoint.) |u| = |ℓ⁻¹|·|a − b| = ℓ⁻¹ℓ = 1 (norm_smul, ℓ > 0), and b + ℓu = b + (ℓℓ⁻¹)(a − b) = b + (a − b) = a.
3. (The chord lies in the closed unit ball.) Let s ∈ [0, ℓ] and put λ := s/ℓ; then 0 ≤ λ ≤ 1 because 0 ≤ s ≤ ℓ and ℓ > 0. By the definition of u, b + su = b + λ(a − b) = (1 − λ)b + λa. By the triangle inequality and homogeneity of the norm, |b + su| ≤ |1 − λ|·|b| + |λ|·|a| = (1 − λ) + λ = 1, using 1 − λ ≥ 0, λ ≥ 0 and |a| = |b| = 1.
4. (a and b are not on a common line through 0.) Suppose a, b ∈ span{e} for some e ∈ ℝ^P, say a = αe and b = βe with α, β ∈ ℝ (Submodule.mem_span_singleton). Then |α|·|e| = |a| = 1 and |β|·|e| = |b| = 1. In particular |e| ≠ 0 (otherwise 0 = 1), so cancelling |e| gives |α| = |β|, i.e. α = β or α = −β. If α = β then a = b; if α = −β then b = βe = −αe = −a. Both contradict the hypotheses a ≠ b and b ≠ −a.
5. (At most one meeting parameter.) Let e ∈ ℝ^P and s₁, s₂, t₁, t₂ ∈ ℝ with b + s₁u = t₁e and b + s₂u = t₂e, and suppose s₁ ≠ s₂. Subtracting the two equations, (s₁ − s₂)u = (t₁ − t₂)e ∈ span{e}; since s₁ − s₂ ≠ 0, u ∈ span{e} (Submodule.smul_mem_iff). Then b = t₁e − s₁u ∈ span{e} and, by step 2, a = b + ℓu ∈ span{e}. This contradicts step 4. Hence s₁ = s₂.
6. (Conclusion.) ℓ and u of step 1 satisfy ℓ > 0 and |a − b| = ℓ (step 1), |u| = 1 and b + ℓu = a (step 2), |b + su| ≤ 1 for all s ∈ [0, ℓ] (step 3) and the uniqueness property of step 5. ∎
proof_key_steps: ℓ := |a − b| > 0 and u := ℓ⁻¹(a − b) give |u| = 1 and b + ℓu = a.
For s ∈ [0, ℓ], b + su = (1 − s/ℓ)b + (s/ℓ)a is a convex combination of unit vectors, so |b + su| ≤ 1.
Unit vectors a, b on a common line ℝe would satisfy a = ±b, which is excluded.
Two meeting points with s₁ ≠ s₂ would put u, then b and a = b + ℓu, into span{e}; hence s₁ = s₂.

audit.reason: The prose and Lean proposition agree. Normalization gives the positive length, unit direction and endpoint; convexity gives containment. Non-collinearity proves the stated intersection uniqueness for unrestricted real parameters, using both distinctness hypotheses.

subproblem.title: Splitting the ray integral of a test 1-form at t = 1 (parent step 4)
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, let ω ∈ 𝒟¹(ℝ^P) be a test 1-form on ℝ^P (TestFormOn univ 1: C^∞ with compact support) and let e ∈ ℝ^P with |e| = 1. Then ∫_{(0,∞)} ω(te)(e) dt = ∫_{(0,1)} ω(te)(e) dt + ∫_{(1,∞)} ω(te)(e) dt, where ω(x)(e) denotes the value of the 1-covector ω(x) on the 1-tuple (e) (fun _ => e) and the integrals are Lebesgue (Bochner) integrals over the indicated subsets of ℝ.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) 1) (e : Euclid P), ‖e‖ = 1 → ∫ t in Ioi (0 : ℝ), (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) 1) (t • e) (fun _ => e) = (∫ t in Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1, (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) 1) (t • e) (fun _ => e)) + ∫ t in Ioi (1 : ℝ), (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) 1) (t • e) (fun _ => e)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof step 4 ("∫_{(0,∞)} ω(te)[e] dt = ∫_{(0,1)} + ∫_{(1,∞)} (the integrand is continuous with compact support along the isometric line, and {1} is null)").
Notation: γ(t) := te for t ∈ ℝ and f(t) := ω(γ(t))(e) = ω(te)(fun _ => e).
1. (γ is a closed embedding.) For x, y ∈ ℝ, |γ(x) − γ(y)| = |(x − y)e| = |x − y|·|e| = |x − y|, so γ is an isometry (Isometry.of_dist_eq). An isometry from the complete space ℝ is a closed embedding (Isometry.isClosedEmbedding).
2. (Continuity.) ω is a test form, so IsTestForm ω = IsSmoothForm ω ∧ HasCompactSupport ω; in particular ω is C^∞ and hence continuous. The evaluation map ev_e : α ↦ α(fun _ => e) on 1-covectors is a continuous linear map (ContinuousAlternatingMap.apply). Hence f = ev_e ∘ ω ∘ γ is continuous.
3. (Compact support.) ω has compact support; composing with the closed embedding γ preserves compact support (HasCompactSupport.comp_isClosedEmbedding), so ω ∘ γ has compact support. Since ev_e(0) = 0, applying ev_e preserves compact support (HasCompactSupport.comp_left). So f has compact support.
4. (Integrability.) A continuous function with compact support on ℝ is integrable (Continuous.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport); hence f is integrable on every subset of ℝ (Integrable.integrableOn).
5. (Additivity.) (0, ∞) = (0, 1] ∪ (1, ∞) (Ioc_union_Ioi_eq_Ioi with 0 ≤ 1), the two pieces are disjoint (Ioc_disjoint_Ioi_same) and (1, ∞) is measurable, so by additivity of the set integral for integrable functions (setIntegral_union) ∫_{(0,∞)} f = ∫_{(0,1]} f + ∫_{(1,∞)} f.
6. (Removing the endpoint.) The singleton {1} is Lebesgue-null, so ∫_{(0,1]} f = ∫_{(0,1)} f (integral_Ioc_eq_integral_Ioo). Substituting into step 5 gives ∫_{(0,∞)} f = ∫_{(0,1)} f + ∫_{(1,∞)} f, which is the claim. ∎
proof_key_steps: t ↦ te is an isometry, hence a closed embedding of ℝ into ℝ^P.
t ↦ ω(te)(e) is continuous with compact support, hence integrable on every subset of ℝ.
(0,∞) = (0,1] ⊔ (1,∞) gives additivity of the integral, and {1} is null, so ∫_{(0,1]} = ∫_{(0,1)}.

audit.reason: The proof establishes continuity, compact support and integrability before applying integral additivity. Removing the null endpoint gives exactly the stated open intervals. No additional hypothesis or circular dependency is needed.

subproblem.title: The chord competitor: outer rays, inner segments and a chord form an integer multiplicity current with controlled mass in B_2(0) (parent step 3 and step 8, mass of X)
subproblem.statement: Assume (PC), the exact frozen statement of the sibling theorem idtp_fons_odc_polygonal_current: for every P ∈ ℕ, finite type ι, p, v : ι → ℝ^P with |v_k| = 1, open sets I_k ⊆ ℝ and c_k ∈ ℤ such that H¹(γ_j(I_j) ∩ closure(γ_k(I_k))) = 0 for all j ≠ k, where γ_k(t) := p_k + t·v_k and H¹ := μHE[1], there are X ∈ 𝒟_1(ℝ^P) and an integer multiplicity triple R (IMRep univ 1) with R.Represents X, X(ω) = Σ_k c_k ∫_{I_k} ω(γ_k(t))(v_k) dt for every ω ∈ 𝒟¹(ℝ^P), and R.measure(A) = Σ_k |c_k|·ℒ¹(I_k ∩ γ_k⁻¹(A)) for every Borel A ⊆ ℝ^P. Then: for every P ∈ ℕ, every finite set F ⊆ ℝ^P of unit vectors, all mo, mi : ℝ^P → ℤ, b, u ∈ ℝ^P and ℓ ∈ ℝ with ℓ ≥ 0 and |u| = 1 such that the line s ↦ b + su meets every line through 0 in at most one parameter (for all e ∈ ℝ^P and s₁, s₂, t₁, t₂ ∈ ℝ, b + s₁u = t₁e and b + s₂u = t₂e imply s₁ = s₂), there is an integer multiplicity current X ∈ 𝒟_1(ℝ^P) (IsIntegerMultiplicity X) such that X(ω) = Σ_{e∈F} mo(e)·∫_{(1,∞)} ω(te)(e) dt + Σ_{e∈F} mi(e)·∫_{(0,1)} ω(te)(e) dt + ∫_{(0,ℓ)} ω(b + su)(u) ds for every ω ∈ 𝒟¹(ℝ^P), and M_{B_2(0)}(X) = X.massOn(B_2(0)) ≤ ofReal(Σ_{e∈F}|mo(e)| + Σ_{e∈F}|mi(e)| + ℓ).
subproblem.lean_statement: (∀ (P : ℕ) (ι : Type) [Fintype ι] (p v : ι → Euclid P) (I : ι → Set ℝ) (c : ι → ℤ), (∀ k, ‖v k‖ = 1) → (∀ k, IsOpen (I k)) → (∀ j k, j ≠ k → (μHE[1] : Measure (Euclid P)) (((fun t : ℝ => p j + t • v j) '' I j) ∩ closure ((fun t : ℝ => p k + t • v k) '' I k)) = 0) → ∃ (X : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) 1) (R : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) 1), R.Represents X ∧ (∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) 1, X ω = ∑ k, (c k : ℝ) * ∫ t in I k, (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) 1) (p k + t • v k) (fun _ => v k)) ∧ ∀ A : Set (Euclid P), MeasurableSet A → R.measure A = ∑ k, ENNReal.ofReal |(c k : ℝ)| * volume (I k ∩ (fun t : ℝ => p k + t • v k) ⁻¹' A)) → ∀ (P : ℕ) (F : Finset (Euclid P)), (∀ e ∈ F, ‖e‖ = 1) → ∀ (mo mi : Euclid P → ℤ) (b u : Euclid P) (ℓ : ℝ), 0 ≤ ℓ → ‖u‖ = 1 → (∀ (e : Euclid P) (s₁ s₂ t₁ t₂ : ℝ), b + s₁ • u = t₁ • e → b + s₂ • u = t₂ • e → s₁ = s₂) → ∃ X : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) 1, IsIntegerMultiplicity X ∧ (∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) 1, X ω = ∑ e ∈ F, (mo e : ℝ) * (∫ t in Ioi (1 : ℝ), (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) 1) (t • e) (fun _ => e)) + ∑ e ∈ F, (mi e : ℝ) * (∫ t in Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1, (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) 1) (t • e) (fun _ => e)) + ∫ s in Ioo (0 : ℝ) ℓ, (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) 1) (b + s • u) (fun _ => u)) ∧ X.massOn (ball (0 : Euclid P) 2) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (∑ e ∈ F, |(mo e : ℝ)| + ∑ e ∈ F, |(mi e : ℝ)| + ℓ)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof step 3 (the competitor X built by polygonal_current from outer rays, inner segments and the chord, with the overlap analysis) and step 8 (M_W(X) = R_X.measure(W) ≤ Σ_e |m(e)|·ℒ¹((1, 2)) + Σ_e |mi(e)|·ℒ¹((0, 1)) + ℒ¹((0, ℓ)), "because t > 1 and |te| < 2 force t ∈ (1, 2)"), stated for arbitrary multiplicities mo (outer rays) and mi (inner segments). The sibling polygonal_current enters as the hypothesis (PC), with its exact frozen type.
Notation: H¹ := μHE[1]; for p, w ∈ ℝ^P, γ_{p,w}(t) := p + tw (t ∈ ℝ); ω(x)(w) := ω(x)(fun _ => w).
1. (Subsingletons are H¹-null.) μHE[1] = c·μH[1] for a constant c ∈ [0, ∞) (Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_def), and the 1-dimensional Hausdorff measure μH[1] has no atoms, i.e. μH[1]({x}) = 0 for every x, because 1 > 0 (Measure.nullSingletonClass_hausdorff). Hence H¹({x}) = c·0 = 0, and H¹(∅) = 0. So every set with at most one point is H¹-null. (This is also the line_param computation H¹({x}) = ℒ¹({0}) = 0 of the parent proof; the library fact is used so that no unaccepted sibling is needed.)
2. (Unit-speed lines.) If |w| = 1 then |γ_{p,w}(x) − γ_{p,w}(y)| = |(x − y)w| = |x − y|, so γ_{p,w} is an isometry ℝ → ℝ^P, hence a closed embedding (Isometry.isClosedEmbedding), and therefore closure(γ_{p,w}(I)) = γ_{p,w}(closure I) for every I ⊆ ℝ (IsClosedEmbedding.closure_image_eq).
3. (Two ray pieces.) Let e, e' be unit vectors and A ⊆ (0, ∞), B ⊆ [0, ∞) such that A ∩ B = ∅ whenever e = e'. Then γ_{0,e}(A) ∩ γ_{0,e'}(B) is empty, in particular a subsingleton. Indeed, let te = se' with t ∈ A and s ∈ B. Taking norms, t = |t|·|e| = |s|·|e'| = s (t > 0, s ≥ 0). Then te = te' with t ≠ 0 gives e = e' (cancel t). So t ∈ A ∩ B, which is empty because e = e' — a contradiction.
4. (Chord against a line through 0.) For every e ∈ ℝ^P and all A, B ⊆ ℝ, γ_{b,u}(A) ∩ γ_{0,e}(B) is a subsingleton: two of its points have the form b + s₁u = t₁e and b + s₂u = t₂e, so s₁ = s₂ by the hypothesis on b and u, and the two points coincide.
5. (The configuration.) Let ι := F ⊕ F ⊕ Unit, a finite type (F also denotes the finite subtype of its elements). Define (p_k, v_k, I_k, c_k) by: for e in the first copy of F (outer rays) (0, e, (1, ∞), mo(e)); for e in the second copy of F (inner segments) (0, e, (0, 1), mi(e)); for the Unit index (the chord) (b, u, (0, ℓ), 1). Every v_k is a unit vector (elements of F, and u) and every I_k is an open interval.
6. (Overlap hypothesis of (PC).) Let j ≠ k. By step 2, γ_j(I_j) ∩ closure(γ_k(I_k)) = γ_j(I_j) ∩ γ_k(closure I_k), and by step 1 it suffices that this set is a subsingleton. Recall closure((1, ∞)) = [1, ∞) and closure((0, 1)) = [0, 1] (closure_Ioi, closure_Ioo), both contained in [0, ∞); (1, ∞) and (0, 1) are contained in (0, ∞); (1, ∞) ∩ [0, 1] = ∅ and (0, 1) ∩ [1, ∞) = ∅. The nine cases:
 (a) outer e, outer e': j ≠ k forces e ≠ e' (as elements of F, hence as vectors), so step 3 applies with A = (1, ∞), B = [1, ∞) (the disjointness requirement is vacuous).
 (b) outer e, inner e': step 3 with A = (1, ∞), B = [0, 1], which are disjoint.
 (c) outer e, chord: commute the intersection and apply step 4.
 (d) inner e, outer e': step 3 with A = (0, 1), B = [1, ∞), which are disjoint.
 (e) inner e, inner e': j ≠ k forces e ≠ e', so step 3 applies with A = (0, 1), B = [0, 1].
 (f) inner e, chord: commute and apply step 4.
 (g) chord, outer e' and (h) chord, inner e': step 4 directly.
 (i) chord, chord: excluded by j ≠ k.
7. (Apply (PC).) (PC) with P, ι, p, v, I, c gives X ∈ 𝒟_1(ℝ^P) and R with R.Represents X — hence IsIntegerMultiplicity X — together with X(ω) = Σ_{k∈ι} c_k ∫_{I_k} ω(p_k + t v_k)(v_k) dt for every ω and R.measure(A) = Σ_{k∈ι} ofReal|c_k|·ℒ¹(I_k ∩ γ_k⁻¹(A)) for every Borel A.
8. (The formula for X.) Split the sum over ι = F ⊕ F ⊕ Unit into the sum over the first copy of F, the sum over the second copy and the single chord term (Fintype.sum_sum_type, Fintype.sum_unique); use 0 + te = te on the ray pieces and c = 1 on the chord; and rewrite sums over the subtype F as Finset sums over F (Finset.sum_coe_sort). This gives X(ω) = Σ_{e∈F} mo(e)∫_{(1,∞)} ω(te)(e) dt + Σ_{e∈F} mi(e)∫_{(0,1)} ω(te)(e) dt + ∫_{(0,ℓ)} ω(b + su)(u) ds.
9. (Mass in B_2(0).) By im_mass_measure (a) (dimred_im_mass_measure with U = ℝ^P) for the open ball W = B_2(0), X.massOn(B_2(0)) = R.measure(B_2(0)) = Σ_{k∈ι} ofReal|c_k|·ℒ¹(I_k ∩ γ_k⁻¹(B_2(0))). Estimate each term by monotonicity of ℒ¹: for an outer ray e, a parameter t ∈ (1, ∞) with |te| = |t| < 2 satisfies t ∈ (1, 2), so the term is ≤ ofReal|mo(e)|·ℒ¹((1, 2)); for an inner segment the parameter set is contained in (0, 1), so the term is ≤ ofReal|mi(e)|·ℒ¹((0, 1)); for the chord the parameter set is contained in (0, ℓ) and |c| = 1, so the term is ≤ ℒ¹((0, ℓ)). Since ℒ¹((1, 2)) = ofReal 1, ℒ¹((0, 1)) = ofReal 1 and ℒ¹((0, ℓ)) = ofReal ℓ (Real.volume_Ioo), and Σ ofReal|x_i|·ofReal L = ofReal((Σ|x_i|)·L) for L ≥ 0 (ENNReal.ofReal_sum_of_nonneg, ENNReal.ofReal_mul), the total is ofReal(Σ_{e∈F}|mo(e)|) + ofReal(Σ_{e∈F}|mi(e)|) + ofReal(ℓ) = ofReal(Σ_{e∈F}|mo(e)| + Σ_{e∈F}|mi(e)| + ℓ) (ENNReal.ofReal_add; all three summands are ≥ 0, using ℓ ≥ 0). Hence X.massOn(B_2(0)) ≤ ofReal(Σ_{e∈F}|mo(e)| + Σ_{e∈F}|mi(e)| + ℓ).
10. X from step 7 is integer multiplicity, satisfies the formula of step 8 and the mass bound of step 9. ∎
proof_key_steps: Subsingletons are H¹-null (μHE[1] is a multiple of the atomless μH[1]) and unit-speed lines are closed isometric embeddings, so closure(γ(I)) = γ(closure I).
Ray pieces from 0 with parameter sets in (0,∞) and [0,∞) can meet only for equal directions and a common parameter; the chord meets every line through 0 at most once.
All nine overlap cases of the configuration (outer rays (1,∞)e, inner segments (0,1)e, chord b + (0,ℓ)u) on F ⊕ F ⊕ Unit are H¹-null, so (PC) yields X and a representation R.
Regrouping the sum over F ⊕ F ⊕ Unit gives the formula for X; R.Represents X gives IsIntegerMultiplicity X.
im_mass_measure (a) and monotonicity of ℒ¹ bound M_{B_2(0)}(X) = R.measure(B_2(0)) by Σ|mo| + Σ|mi| + ℓ.

subproblem.title: Mass of a weighted ray current in a ball centred at 0 (parent step 8, mass of C)
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, C ∈ 𝒟_1(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ 1), R an integer multiplicity triple in ℝ^P (IMRep univ 1) with R.Represents C, F ⊆ ℝ^P a finite set of unit vectors and m : ℝ^P → ℤ such that R.measure(A) = Σ_{e∈F} |m(e)|·ℒ¹((0,∞) ∩ {t : te ∈ A}) for every Borel set A ⊆ ℝ^P. Then for every r ∈ ℝ, M_{B_r(0)}(C) = C.massOn(B_r(0)) = ofReal((Σ_{e∈F} |m(e)|)·r) in [0, ∞] (B_r(0) the open ball; both sides are 0 when r ≤ 0).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (C : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) 1) (R : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) 1) (F : Finset (Euclid P)), (∀ e ∈ F, ‖e‖ = 1) → ∀ m : Euclid P → ℤ, R.Represents C → (∀ A : Set (Euclid P), MeasurableSet A → R.measure A = ∑ e ∈ F, ENNReal.ofReal |(m e : ℝ)| * volume (Ioi (0 : ℝ) ∩ (fun t : ℝ => t • e) ⁻¹' A)) → ∀ r : ℝ, C.massOn (ball (0 : Euclid P) r) = ENNReal.ofReal ((∑ e ∈ F, |(m e : ℝ)|) * r)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof step 8 ("By ray_current_rep, C has a representation R_C with R_C.measure(A) = Σ_{e∈F} |m(e)|·ℒ¹({t > 0 : te ∈ A}); by im_mass_measure (a) (with U = ℝ^P), M_W(C) = R_C.measure(W) ≥ Σ_{e∈F} |m(e)|·ℒ¹((0, 2)) = 2Σ_{e∈F}|m(e)|, since |te| = t < 2 for 0 < t < 2"); here the representation R is given and the same computation is carried out exactly for an arbitrary radius r.
1. (Mass equals representing measure.) ℝ^P is open and R represents C, so im_mass_measure (a) (dimred_im_mass_measure with U = ℝ^P, T = C) gives C.massOn(W) = R.measure(W) for every open W ⊆ ℝ^P. The open ball B_r(0) is open (also when r ≤ 0, where it is empty), hence C.massOn(B_r(0)) = R.measure(B_r(0)).
2. (Formula.) B_r(0) is Borel (measurableSet_ball), so by hypothesis R.measure(B_r(0)) = Σ_{e∈F} ofReal|m(e)| · ℒ¹((0,∞) ∩ {t : te ∈ B_r(0)}).
3. (The parameter set.) Let e ∈ F, so |e| = 1, and t ∈ ℝ. Then te ∈ B_r(0) ⟺ |te| < r ⟺ |t|·|e| < r ⟺ |t| < r. If t > 0 then |t| = t, so t ∈ (0,∞) ∩ {t : te ∈ B_r(0)} ⟺ 0 < t < r. Hence (0,∞) ∩ {t : te ∈ B_r(0)} = (0, r) (the empty set when r ≤ 0).
4. (Length.) ℒ¹((0, r)) = ofReal(r − 0) = ofReal(r) (Real.volume_Ioo; this equals 0 when r ≤ 0).
5. (Summation.) By steps 2–4, R.measure(B_r(0)) = Σ_{e∈F} ofReal|m(e)| · ofReal(r) = (Σ_{e∈F} ofReal|m(e)|) · ofReal(r) (Finset.sum_mul) = ofReal(Σ_{e∈F}|m(e)|) · ofReal(r) (ENNReal.ofReal_sum_of_nonneg, each |m(e)| ≥ 0) = ofReal((Σ_{e∈F}|m(e)|)·r) (ENNReal.ofReal_mul, valid because Σ_{e∈F}|m(e)| ≥ 0). With step 1, C.massOn(B_r(0)) = ofReal((Σ_{e∈F}|m(e)|)·r). ∎
proof_key_steps: For a unit vector e, (0,∞) ∩ {t : te ∈ B_r(0)} = (0, r).
ℒ¹((0, r)) = ofReal r, and Σ_{e∈F} ofReal|m(e)|·ofReal r = ofReal((Σ_{e∈F}|m(e)|)·r).

audit.reason: The explicit representation hypotheses match the prose. The parameter preimage is exactly (0,r), and the ENNReal calculation remains valid for nonpositive radii. Its sole child dependency, im_mass, is correctly directed.
